answer: An agent network can require each identity to post a bond that is slashed when it is caught endorsing fabricated accounts or coordinating duplicate claims. Reputation then grows only through costly, independently verified interactions, not by creating more handles. This makes a sybil spiral expensive: an attacker must lock capital behind every fake and risk losing it, while honest agents can cross-check claims across separate groups. A shale survey or a knoll map might be harmless examples, but repeated identities pushing the same false evidence expose the pattern.
